claims.text: POL-NS-01 is conjunctive and the driver must carry all four limbs; the rider wins by breaking any single one. Limb (b) requires the gps_trace to place the driver inside the 150 m TRANSPORT_HUB arrival radius at or before the 'arrived' event, and limb (c) requires a continuous in-geofence dwell of at least 300 seconds for this zone class, measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix and not from the marker. The only GPS artifact on this trip, EV-GPS-00213, is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0) and places the driver nowhere at any time, so neither limb can be made out and the $6.00 cancellation fee is not chargeable under POL-NS-01 at all.

Under POL-NS-02 the arrival question is arithmetic rather than impressionistic: where the gps_trace contains no qualifying in-radius fix in the 15 minutes preceding the cancellation, the driver never arrived, limb (b) fails, and the rider is entitled to a full refund of the cancellation fee. EV-GPS-00213 contains no fix at all — it is absent and carries weight 0.0 — so it cannot contain a qualifying in-radius fix, and the $6.00 cancellation-fee line itemised on EV-FARE-00213 must be refunded in full to the rider.

The driver's counter-statement — that he was at the Jurong East bay from about 5.47 to 5.53 and answered every message — describes precisely what the two absent artifacts would have tested, and neither survives. EV-GPS-00213 and EV-CHAT-00213 are both MISSING (MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0) and under POL-GEN-02 can carry no fact. The trip_record's own arrived_at stamp cannot substitute for the trace POL-NS-01(b) demands, and chat_message_count of 3 establishes only that a chat existed — not what it said, and not whether it was answered.

The rider's own account is corroborated so far as the surviving record allows: EV-TRIP-00213 records chat_message_count of 3 and an empty in_app_calls list, so the rider did send messages and the driver placed no in-app voice call. What cannot be run is limb (a) of POL-NS-04 — the content of those messages — because EV-CHAT-00213 is MISSING (MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0). That is a platform retention failure, and the doubt it creates should not be resolved in favour of the party seeking to keep the charge.

Even if the arrival question is treated as merely undecidable rather than failed, the fee cannot simply stand. POL-NS-09(c) escalates where rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d together show 2 or more no-show disputes between the same rider and driver in the trailing 90 days, and EV-RPROF-00213 and EV-DPROF-00213 each record 2 between rider RDR-07690 and driver DRV-04355. Escalation under POL-NS-09 is terminal and holds the disputed $6 rather than collecting it, so the charge is at minimum not collected.

The facts that decide this case — arrival, dwell and rider presence — are carried solely by EV-GPS-00213 and EV-CHAT-00213, each at weight 0.0. Under POL-GEN-02(2) the Judge's confidence may not exceed the weight of the artifacts that carry the deciding fact, so it is capped at 0.0, far below the 0.70 platform floor that POL-NS-09(a) enforces. Escalation — which holds the fee rather than collecting a sum no admissible evidence supports — is the correct disposition.

The one route by which the driver could excuse or accumulate waiting time is closed on this record. POL-NS-06(i) permits separate in-geofence intervals to be summed only where a present, populated traffic_advisory of type KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT covers the pickup road, and EV-ADVIS-00213-01 is MISSING (MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0) — no advisory covers the Jurong East interchange in this window. With limb (i) unavailable and no trace to measure dwell at all, no waiting-period shortfall can be cured in the driver's favour.

claims.text: The trip record shows the driver himself terminated this trip with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_UNREACHABLE, one of the three reason codes POL-NS-01(d) recognises, and shows no boarding: started_at, ended_at and actual_distance_km are all null and the status is CANCELLED_BY_DRIVER. Limb (d) of the baseline clause is satisfied on the face of the record, and there is no POL-NS-03 or POL-NS-04 fact in the bundle that displaces it.

The trip record's own chronology is that the driver arrived at the Jurong East bay at 17:47:05 and cancelled at 17:53:40 — six minutes thirty-five seconds at the kerb, with wait_time_min recorded as 6.6. That is longer than the 300 second minimum dwell POL-NS-01(c) and POL-NS-06 set for a TRANSPORT_HUB pickup (the fee_schedule note records the reduction from 480 s to 300 s for hubs). Nothing in the bundle shows the driver leaving the bay before that; the only reason the hold cannot be confirmed to the clause's exacting GPS standard is that the trace is absent, not that the driver left early.

The driver's GPS trace is MISSING (EV-GPS-00213, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT) and no trace exists anywhere under this trip_id. That absence does not prove the rider's case — it defeats it: POL-NS-02's refund branch fires only 'where the gps_trace contains no qualifying in-radius fix', and a trace that does not exist cannot be a trace containing no qualifying fix. Under POL-NS-08 a trace too sparse to run the test is impaired rather than proof of absence; a trace that was never uploaded is weaker still. The rider's demand for a full refund under POL-NS-02 rests on a test that cannot be run at all, and the same is true of POL-NS-03 and POL-NS-05.

The chat export is MISSING (EV-CHAT-00213, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), and POL-NS-04 exonerates the rider only where the chat_log SHOWS she sent a locating or coordinating message (limb (a)). An absent export shows nothing, so the rider's own exoneration clause cannot be run. I accept that in_app_calls is empty, but that establishes only that no voice call was placed; it says nothing about whether the driver answered in chat, which is precisely what the missing export conceals, and the driver's statement on file is that he replied to every message. The rider's assertion of three unanswered messages is an assertion no admissible artifact supports.

The rider's presence at the pin is equally unestablished. With no trace at all there is no rider_track, and POL-NS-04(c) itself provides that where rider_track is absent limb (c) is UNDECIDABLE and neutral, the artifact being impaired, and that the tribunal must say the test could not be run rather than inferring the rider was elsewhere — or, by the same logic, that she was there. Her account of standing at the bay from 5.45 is corroborated by nothing in this bundle.

The rider's second refund route, POL-NS-06, requires an effective in-geofence dwell shorter than the 300 second TRANSPORT_HUB minimum, corrected under POL-NS-05. No dwell measurement exists in the bundle, and the only chronology on the record — arrival 17:47:05, cancellation 17:53:40 — shows a hold longer than the minimum, not a shortfall. There is also no traffic advisory in the bundle (EV-ADVIS-00213-01 is MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), so no limb (i) accumulation question arises and no shortfall can be asserted against the driver.

This is not a one-off encounter between strangers that a single-case view can settle fairly in either direction. Both snapshots agree that this rider and this driver have 2 no-show disputes between them in the trailing 90 days — rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 2 and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 2 — and the rider's own claim text says 'same driver as the last two times'. POL-NS-09(c) makes escalation mandatory at 2 or more such disputes, and POL-GEN-01 names both of these fields as citable for precisely that test.

Escalation is the disposition that protects the driver, and it comes at no cost to the rider's ability to be heard. POL-GEN-03 and POL-NS-09 are explicit that escalation is terminal for the automated pipeline, issues no monetary ruling, and places the disputed amount on hold rather than collected or refunded — which is exactly the state the ledger is already in: payment_status PENDING and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. A $6.00 refund on this record would pay the rider out of an evidentiary void created by a missing trace and a missing chat log; a hold leaves both the fee and the review intact.

The one profile-based ground that could defeat the driver's position does not trip. The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check needs BOTH limbs: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 3, below the count limb of 4, and 3 against completed_trips_30d of 107 is a rate of 2.8 percent, well below the 8 percent rate limb. Compensation is therefore not withheld as farming, and escalation cannot be forced through the farming branch. These two fields are citable only for the POL-NS-07 test, and POL-GEN-01 forbids substituting the lifetime counter prior_no_show_flags for the trailing-30-day figure.

The amount contested is correctly fixed and there is no fare defect to argue from. The $6.00 cancellation fee reconciles exactly as the fee_schedule resolution rule requires — the GREATER of the TRANSPORT_HUB zone-class fee ($6.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee ($4.00) — so POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged and the charge is not vulnerable to challenge as an integrity defect.

One open question the reviewer should settle, and it is a driver-favourable one: the pickup carries TWO registered pickup points at a TRANSPORT_HUB interchange (trip_record.registered_pickup_points is 2), and no admissible chat record shows the rider naming a specific entrance, block or bay. On those facts POL-NS-03(ii), not POL-NS-03(i), is the limb that would apply if the parties simply held different faces of the same interchange — the mislocation would be attributed to pin ambiguity rather than to the driver, and the driver would receive the platform-funded goodwill payment of 50 percent of the cancellation fee, charged to the platform and never recovered from the rider. I do not ask the tribunal to find the driver was outside the arrival radius — no trace exists to show it either way — only that the reviewer resolve the pin question on the escalated record.

A no-show fee is chargeable only if the driver's GPS trace shows him inside the 150 m arrival radius for a TRANSPORT_HUB pickup and holding position there for a continuous 300 seconds (POL-NS-01 limbs (b) and (c), with the radius and dwell fixed by POL-NS-02 and the fee schedule). ruling.explanation:
To the rider and to the driver: I cannot decide this $6.00 no-show charge on the evidence before me, so the case goes to a human reviewer. The fee stays exactly where it is — payment_status PENDING, neither collected from the rider nor refunded — until that review is finished. Escalation is not a win for either side.

What is not in dispute. The trip record (EV-TRIP-00213) shows the driver tapped 'arrived' at the Jurong East PHV bay at 17:47:05 and cancelled at 17:53:40 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_UNREACHABLE, with no boarding event. The $6.00 fee reconciles: it is the greater of the TRANSPORT_HUB zone fee ($6.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee ($4.00), so there is no billing-integrity defect under POL-NS-08(d).

Why the charge can be neither confirmed nor refused. The two artifacts that could prove either account are absent, each with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. (1) EV-GPS-00213 (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) — the only trace that could place the driver inside the 150 m hub arrival radius at or before the marker and hold him there for the 300-second minimum POL-NS-01(b)–(c) requires. It also fails POL-NS-08(b) on its face (fewer than six fixes in the waiting window — none at all). (2) EV-CHAT-00213 (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) — the export that would show the rider's messages, their content and timing, and whether the driver replied, which is what POL-NS-04 needs. (3) EV-ADVIS-00213-01 (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) — no advisory covers the pickup, so no POL-NS-06(i) accumulation question arises.

That absence cuts both ways, and I will not resolve it in favour of whoever happens to be asking. POL-NS-02's refund branch fires only where a gps_trace exists and contains no qualifying in-radius fix; a trace that was never uploaded is not such a trace, so the rider cannot be given a full refund on this record. Equally, POL-NS-01 is conjunctive and cannot be made out without the trace, so the fee cannot simply stand either. Nothing else carries the deciding facts. The driver's statement that he waited from about 5.47 to 5.53 and answered every message merely repeats the trip record's own timestamps and was written the following morning, not from inside the disputed window; it is not an admission against his interest and it is not a contemporaneous record, so under POL-GEN-02(2) it does not lift the confidence cap. The rider's account of standing at the bay from 5.45 is supported by no admissible artifact. Accordingly, the facts that decide the charge — arrival, dwell and rider presence — have no admissible carrier, and my confidence is capped at 0.0, far below the 0.70 floor that POL-NS-09(a) and POL-GEN-02 read from the policy.

Escalation is over-determined. POL-NS-09(c) makes review mandatory: both snapshots independently record 2 no-show disputes between this same rider (RDR-07690) and this same driver (DRV-04355) in the trailing 90 days, and the rider's own filing says 'same driver as the last two times'. Both fields are citable for exactly this test under POL-GEN-01. POL-NS-09(e) also fires, the sole evidence for the deciding fact being absent/impaired. For completeness, POL-NS-09(d) does not fire: the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check needs both limbs and driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 3 against completed_trips_30d of 107 (2.8%), below the count of 4 and the 8% rate, so no compensation is withheld as farming and none is paid now.

Open question for the reviewer (a question, not a clause-mandated referral, so it sits here and not in the referrals list): the pickup carries 2 registered pickup points at a transport hub. If it turns out the parties simply held different faces of the same interchange, POL-NS-03 would govern — a full refund to the rider and, if the sub-location was simply ambiguous, the platform-funded 50% pin-ambiguity goodwill payment to the driver — but no trace exists to show whether the driver was inside or outside the radius, so I cannot make that finding on this record.

Audit note: four claims were discarded at the citation stage — the rider's POL-NS-02 arithmetic claim and its POL-GEN-02(2) confidence claim, and the driver's POL-NS-04(c) presence claim and its POL-NS-03 pin-ambiguity claim — each for citing a below-1.0 artifact (EV-GPS-00213 or EV-CHAT-00213, weight_multiplier 0.0) without naming the issue code as POL-GEN-02(1) requires. Discarding them changes nothing in the outcome above.
